main_text.p: retinet, pro ea parte naturalem obliga tionem fublatam effe. Quum enim na tura Marco fuum peculiu conferuet, pater autem illud cōtra naturae legem retineat: fine dubio, natura ei ius illud obligationis in filium quaesitum, pro parte retēti peculiį adimit. Doceamus nunc, adeptione sui iuris & emancipa tione naturalem obligationem nō ex tingui. probat id Africanus argumen to ex effectis: Si filiusfamilias, inquit, extraneo aliquid debeat, poteft extra neus intra mancipationis annum in pa trem ex peculio agere. l. 1, D. quando act. de pecul. At si agat extraneus, po teft pater, quod sibi filius debuit, dedu cere. l. 9, §. 3, de pecul. Ex quo facile in tellectu eft, naturalem obligationem etiam poft emancipationem manere. Nam quo tandem iure pater deducet? nimirū obligationis naturalis. Quem admodum ergo recte sic cōcludimus: Si sol lucet, dies est (lux enim solis, diei causa est cōficiens) similiter hocmodo recte possumus: Si deducēdi detrahen diꝙ [?] debiti patri facultas est, naturalis subest obligatio. quippe quae causa il-lius

page.notes: The running head is partly blurred and could not be read; the approximate length is estimated. The word at the start of "detrahen diꝙ" is doubtful; the second word is uncertain (read as diꝙ, possibly dicꝙ). The final word is split as "il-" and "lius" across the last line and the bottom of the page. A small reference mark "y" stands at the foot of the page left of "lius"; no matching note is printed on this page. Some lines show show-through from the reverse side and are not transcribed.
